q: The SI unit of force is:
Force is measured in newtons. One newton accelerates a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s².
The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
Light travels at about 299,792,458 m/s, commonly rounded to 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
At sea level, pure water boils at:
At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100°C. At higher altitudes it boils at a lower temperature.
The chemical symbol Na stands for:
Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium. Its atomic number is 11.
A solution with pH less than 7 is:
pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. This explains rocket propulsion.
Ohm's law relates voltage, current and:
V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current and R is resistance.
The hardest naturally occurring substance is:
Diamond is a form of carbon with a very strong tetrahedral lattice, making it the hardest natural material.
The gas that gives fizzy drinks their bubbles is:
Carbon dioxide dissolves under pressure and forms bubbles when the pressure is released.
Iron rusts when exposed to oxygen and water, forming hydrated iron oxide.
The atomic number of an element equals the number of:
Atomic number is the number of protons. In a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons.
Sound needs a medium. In a vacuum there are no particles to carry the vibrations.
A concave lens diverges light so the image forms on the retina instead of in front of it.
Which form of carbon conducts electricity?
Graphite has delocalised electrons in layers, so it conducts electricity. Diamond does not.
Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere; oxygen is about 21%.
The largest organ of the human body is:
Skin is the largest organ by surface area and protects the body from infection and injury.
Red blood cells carry oxygen using:
Haemoglobin, an iron-containing protein, binds oxygen in the lungs and carries it to tissues.
Insulin is produced by which organ?
Insulin is produced by beta cells of the pancreas and regulates blood sugar.
Scurvy causes bleeding gums and poor wound healing. Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C.
Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin with the help of:
Ultraviolet light helps the skin make vitamin D, which is needed for calcium absorption.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and usually affects the lungs.
Which blood group is called the universal donor?
O negative red cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be given to most patients in emergencies.
The human heart has how many chambers?
The heart has two atria and two ventricles. The left ventricle pumps blood to the body.
Photosynthesis in plants takes place mainly in:
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.
Watson and Crick described DNA as a double helix held together by base pairs.
The largest gland in the human body is the:
The liver is the largest gland; it produces bile and performs many metabolic functions.
Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
Killing all bacteria in the body
Vaccines expose the immune system to a harmless antigen so it can remember and fight the real pathogen.
Kidneys filter blood, remove waste and regulate water, salt and acid balance.
Normal human body temperature is about:
Normal core body temperature is around 37°C (98.6°F), though it varies slightly.
Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876.
The practical electric light bulb is associated with:
Thomas Edison developed a commercially practical incandescent bulb in 1879.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928; it became the first widely used antibiotic.
The polio vaccine was developed by:
Jonas Salk developed the first effective polio vaccine in the 1950s.
Marconi is credited with practical wireless telegraphy and radio communication.
The telescope was used by Galileo to study the heavens; it was invented in:
The telescope was invented in the Netherlands around 1608; Galileo improved it and made astronomical observations.
The printing press with movable type was developed by:
Gutenberg's printing press in the 15th century revolutionised the spread of knowledge.
The steam engine was significantly improved by:
James Watt improved the Newcomen engine's efficiency, a key step in the Industrial Revolution.
Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
The theory of relativity is associated with:
Einstein's special and general relativity transformed our understanding of space, time and gravity.
The periodic table was first published by:
Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic weight and predicted undiscovered elements.
The structure of DNA was described by:
James Watson and Francis Crick published the double-helix model in 1953, using Rosalind Franklin's data.
J. J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode ray experiments.
The first powered aeroplane flight was made by:
Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first sustained powered flight in 1903.
The smallpox vaccine was developed by:
Edward Jenner used cowpox material in 1796 to protect against smallpox.
Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing near the Moon's:
India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023, a first for any country.
Aditya-L1 is India's mission to study:
Aditya-L1 studies the Sun from the L1 Lagrange point, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
Gaganyaan aims to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit aboard an Indian launch vehicle.
India's Mars Orbiter Mission, Mangalyaan, was launched in:
Mangalyaan launched in November 2013 and entered Mars orbit in September 2014.
NISAR is a joint Earth-observation satellite of India and:
NISAR is a NASA-ISRO synthetic aperture radar mission to monitor Earth's surface changes.
CRISPR-Cas9 is a technology used for:
CRISPR-Cas9 allows precise editing of DNA sequences, with applications in medicine and agriculture.
5G offers faster data speeds, lower latency and more connected devices than 4G.
The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in:
Webb's infrared instruments can see through dust and study the early universe.
NASA's Artemis programme aims to return humans to:
Artemis aims to land astronauts on the Moon and build toward future Mars missions.
Quantum computers use qubits, which can exist in superpositions of 0 and 1.
mRNA vaccines work by instructing cells to produce:
A viral protein that triggers immunity
mRNA vaccines deliver genetic instructions for a spike protein, training the immune system.
The India Semiconductor Mission supports fabrication and packaging plants to strengthen the electronics supply chain.
Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable electricity, producing no direct carbon emissions.
NavIC provides positioning and timing services over India and the surrounding region.
Aditya-L1, launched in 2023, is India's first dedicated solar observatory mission.
